chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Abu al-A'ala, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man found some wealth, so he announced it (as found property). When a year passed, he bought a servant with it. The seeker of the wealth came and found that the maid who had been bought with the dirhams was his daughter. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not entitled to take except his dirhams, and the daughter is not for him. Rather, he has only the principal of his wealth, and indeed his daughter was a slave owned by people.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on found property used to buy a slave before the owner is found?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction between the original principal (ra's al-mal) and its acquired fruits is clarified, establishing that the owner reclaims the value rather than the specific asset purchased with it. This principle underscores the concept of 'acquisition through exchange' (iktisa') in Shia jurisprudence, where the finder’s use of the funds transfers ownership of the new item to him, leaving the original owner with a claim on the equivalent value. The scenario highlights the practical application of property rights and the separation of capital from its generated utility in cases of found wealth.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from one of our companions, from Abu Al A’ala who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man found some wealth, so he introduced it (to others) until when the year passed by, he bought a servant with it. So the seeker of the wealth came over and found that the maid which had been bought with the Dirhams, she was his daughter’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for him to take except for the Dirhams, and the daughter is not for him. But rather, for him is the capital of his wealth, and rather his daughter would be an owned slave of a people’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain persons of our people from abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘A man found a certain amount of goods and he announced about it in public for one year. He then bought a slave-girl. A man then claiming to be the owner came to him and found the slave-girl who was purchased with that money to be his daughter.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is entitled to take the dirhams but not the slave- girl. The money belongs to him but his daughter is the slave-girl of other people.’”
